newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE STOCKS FINISH ACTIVE DAY MOSTLY FIRMER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE STOCKS FINISH ACTIVE DAY MOSTLY FIRMER.

text.p: Zimbabwean shares continued active and largely firmer on Wednesday as the the first rains of the season in the agriculture-driven country attracted more investors into the stock market.

"We saw some good volumes traded on the market today -- the rains are obviously helping quite nicely, and what with low inflation and low interest rates, I believe this will be the case until well into next year," a broker said.

Counters to advance on Wednesday included blue-chip conglomerate Delta, textile firm David Whitehead, furniture and clothing retailers Tedco, tobacco group TSL, removal group Clan and Flexible Packaging preferentials, which all put on five cents to 3,305, 80, 645 and 610, 305 and 40 respectively.

Pork processor Colcom at 390, seed company Seedco at 220 and tea and coffee producer Tanganda at 310 were all 10 cents firmer, while pharmaceutical group Caps added 15 cents to 370, engineering firm Gulliver went up 20 cents to 230, timber producer Border put on 25 cents to 1,300 and soft-drink company Schweppes edged up 30 cents to 820.
Other gains were in horticulture concern Ariston which traded 50 cents stronger at 1,550 and Zimbabwe Newspapers group, up 200 to 1,800.

Bucking the trend, battery producer Chloride and financial group Finhold both lost five cents to 80 and 970 respectively, Zimbabwe Sugar Refineries (ZSR) shed 20 cents to 1,380 and clothing retailers Edgars went down 200 cents to 3,100.
The 57-counter index put on 28.99 points to close at 8039.92.

Minings were quiet with coal miners Wankie 10 cents firmer at 405 and gold producer Rio Tinto 150 cents up at 3,650, while Falgold, another gold firm shed 2 cents to 133 and nickel company Bindura lost 30 cents to 1,000.
The seven-share mining index added 2.84 points to 1,225.34.
